name:Airway mucus: A shallow translucent mucus sheet has the same oblique surface plane and outline as the top of the airway-cell strip. It contains only its own material.
name:Airway lining with sweeping hairs: A continuous shallow oblique strip of columnar airway cells carries a fringe of fine cilia above its apical surface and a connected basal tissue layer below.
name:Mucus-covered airway lining: A thin translucent mucus blanket follows the apical surface of the same epithelial strip, directly contacting its ciliary tips without crossing the cell bodies.
name:Mucus with trapped particles: The same shallow mucus sheet holds dust grains and small rods within its translucent surface layer.
name:Lung white blood cells: One pale amoeboid macrophage has a kidney-shaped nucleus, granular cytoplasm and small internal vesicles.
name:Lung white cells containing bacteri: The same macrophage contains intact small rod-shaped bacteria inside a clearly bounded cytoplasmic vesicle, separate from the nucleus.
name:Living lymph node: A bean-shaped lymph-node cutaway shows its capsule, densely cellular outer tissue, branching inner tissue and attached vessels as one continuous organ.
name:Responding lymph node: The same lymph-node cutaway contains expanded pale germinal centres and dense populations of descendants embedded within its supporting tissue. No oversized isolated cells cover its surface.
name:Matching antibodies: Several separate Y-shaped antibody proteins retain the same illustrative size used for their bound counterparts.
name:Antibody-coated bacteria: The same three rod-shaped bacteria carry Y-shaped antibody proteins attached by their arm tips to the bacterial surfaces. The stems project outward; no antibody floats apart from a bacterium.
name:Engulfing white blood cells: One pale amoeboid white cell has a kidney-shaped nucleus and clear surrounding cytoplasm with small vesicles.
name:White blood cells containing bacter: The same white cell contains irregular bacterial fragments within a bounded digestive vesicle in its cytoplasm, clearly separate from its nucleus.
